_what: How agent position sizing actually behaves on BattleGrid, measured 2026-09-10 against a real 53.57 USDC wallet with one live position. Written because an assistant leverage recommendation was wrong and the measurement that corrected it is worth keeping.

theMeasurement.claim: feasibilityAdvisory.smallestOrderUsd equals maxConcurrentExposureUsd x maxLeverage. positionSizePresets.smallPct does NOT enter it.
theMeasurement.confidence: Three points, exact fit on all three. The relationship is asserted for these ranges only.

theConsequence.algebra: To hold N concurrent positions you need ceiling >= N x smallestOrderUsd = N x ceiling x leverage, which reduces to N <= 1 / leverage.
theConsequence.soWhat: At leverage 1 the config algebra permits ONE position. At leverage 3 it permits less than one. LEVERAGE MAKES CONCURRENCY WORSE, not better.
theConsequence.theErrorThisCorrects: The assistant recommended 3x leverage on the reasoning that the 10 USD exchange floor applies to NOTIONAL, so leverage would let a position reach it with a third of the margin and thereby free capital for more positions. That reasoning was wrong for this platform: raising leverage raised the minimum order size proportionally.

theOtherConstraint.rule: (smallPct/100) x ceiling x floor(maxLeverage) >= max(10, minAllocationUsd), enforced at config time.
theOtherConstraint.minimumAllocationUsdIsAFloor: 10, from get_trading_config_catalog. It cannot be set lower, so the right-hand side is never below 10.
theOtherConstraint.tension: A LOW smallPct forces a HIGH ceiling x leverage product to satisfy the constraint - and smallestOrderUsd tracks that same product. So asking for small percentage positions mechanically produces LARGE minimum orders. The two rules pull against each other.

whatActuallyBlockedTheTrades.diagnosis: BTC consumed 22.29 of a 25 ceiling, leaving headroom 2.71 against an orderFloorUsd of 10. No further order of any size could fit. All three failures are that, not a bad signal - every one produced a complete bearish thesis and cleared the 0.65 gate (ZEC 86 percent, MOODENG 100 percent composite).
whatActuallyBlockedTheTrades.notTheCause: The correlation with the smallPct 1 -> 45 change is coincidental in timing. With 2.71 of headroom against a 10 USD floor, an order at ANY size fails.
whatActuallyBlockedTheTrades.whereTheReasonIsNOTRecorded: list_gate_blocks showed only one unrelated OPEN_POSITION_CONFLICT. get_agent_journal carried the theses but no error. get_entry_decision carries no error field. The platform does not surface an order-rejection reason on any readable surface - the diagnosis above is arithmetic, not a quoted message.

unresolved: The positionSizePct to notional mapping. positionSizePct 1 produced a 21.617 USD notional, which is not 1 percent of any quantity on this account. Reference-fleet fills contradict each other at the same preset: HYPE 32.45 USD and APT 0.32 USD both at 2 percent MEDIUM.
Whether maxConcurrentExposureUsd is denominated in NOTIONAL or MARGIN. The only fill was at leverage 1, where the two are identical, so it settles nothing.
maxDailyTrades appears not to gate evaluation. tradesToday read 4 against a cap of 2, and decisions 3 and 4 were still evaluated, each burning about 100 seconds of model time.
practicalConclusion: At a 53 USDC wallet against a 10 USD exchange floor, this platform's config algebra permits roughly one open position at a time. The route to more concurrent trades is more capital, not more leverage. The daily-loss stop is the control that actually bounds risk; the ceiling mostly decides position count.

configLeftInPlace.why: Ceiling 30 sits above the 22.29 currently at risk so the budget is not over-subscribed, leverage 1 keeps the minimum order at 30 rather than inflating it, and the 5 USD daily stop caps a bad day at about 9 percent of the wallet.
